text.tspan: Figure 18: Half the training rows lack precipitation type; the power
lags are null once the lead reaches the lag

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'All 31 series. Training: the control member of the 15-month training window. Validation: all 51 ensemble members of the 53 weekly runs, July 2025 to June 2026 (fold A). The upper panel shades each cell by its share of null or NaN values: white is none and orange is all. Precipitation type is null in the first 7 months of the training window, because the stored ECMWF runs of those months carry none. A power lag is null once its lag is no longer than the lead, and also wherever the power history has a gap (6% at 336 hours, days 0 to 2). The lower panel gives each column's minimum, median, and maximum. The power lags are not shown, because their range in megawatts would reveal single generators' sizes.'
text.tspan: All 31 series. Training: the control member of the 15-month training window. Validation: all 51 ensemble members of
the 53 weekly runs, July 2025 to June 2026 (fold A). The upper panel shades each cell by its share of null or NaN
values: white is none and orange is all.
Precipitation type is null in the first 7 months of the training window, because the stored ECMWF runs of those
months carry none. A power lag is null once its lag is no longer than the lead, and also wherever the power history
has a gap (6% at 336 hours, days 0 to 2).
The lower panel gives each column's minimum, median, and maximum. The power lags are not shown, because their range
in megawatts would reveal single generators' sizes.
